functions.quote: Early-years education inspections are carried out in early-years services participating in the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Programme

functions.what: early childhood care and education is delivered outside the formal education system, per this Department
functions.quote: early childhood care and education (ECCE) is delivered outside the formal education system

functions.what: child protection procedures for schools
functions.quote: The Department of Education and Youth is responsible for developing and implementing child protection procedures for schools

functions.quote: department inspectors check that a school is complying with the requirements of the Child Protection Procedures

functions.what: mission
functions.quote: The Department of Education and Youth's mission is to facilitate children and young people, through learning, to achieve their full potential

functions.what: where early learning and childcare and school-age childcare sit: a division of the Department of Children, Disability and Equality (the former DCEDIY), not this Department
functions.quote: Early Learning and Care and School-Age Childcare Division

money.what: allocation: capital funding for UBU Your Place Your Space youth services (minor works and equipment), as announced; 'over' as printed

bodies.notes: gov.ie returns a bot-verification wall (HTTP 403/405) to WebFetch and curl, so every Department page was read from its Internet Archive copy (URLs are the archive copies actually fetched; each is a copy of the Department's own gov.ie page). WHICH DEPARTMENT HOLDS WHAT AFTER 2025: (1) Youth work / UBU funding / youth services: this Department (press release by the 'Minister for Education and Youth'; Education Plan 2025 says 'Youth now transferred into the Department of Education'). (2) Early learning and childcare and school-age childcare: the Department of Children, Disability and Equality (its own about page, last updated 3 December 2025, lists an 'Early Learning and Care and School-Age Childcare Division'; its homepage lists 'Early Learning and Care (ELC) and School-Age Childcare (SAC) Supports'). (3) Not moved with Youth: children and young people's participation in decision-making (Comhairle na nOg, Dail na nOg, National Participation Office) stays with the Department of Children, Disability and Equality ('The Department of Children, Disability and Equality (DCDE) ensures that children and young people have a voice in the design, delivery and monitoring of Government policies', https://web.archive.org/web/20260419153039/https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-children-disability-and-equality/policy-information/youth-participation/ , last updated 10 March 2026). This Department's own policy page describes ECCE as outside the formal education system but names early-years education inspections (who carries them out is not stated in the sentence quoted). The 2025 transfer orders (statutory instruments) were not read; transfer dates seen only in a search summary of Wikipedia are NOT recorded as fact here. The youth/ELC split above rests on the two departments' own current pages. The Education Plan 2025 url is a hosted copy (drugsandalcohol.ie) of the Department's PDF, not the gov.ie original.

bodies.notes: FALLBACK SOURCE: ncca.ie (and ncca.ie/en/about-us/) sits behind a Cloudflare bot-verification wall (HTTP 403 for WebFetch and curl; the in-app browser showed the verification page; not bypassed). bodies.name: The Teaching Council

functions.what: role framed as protecting the public by regulating professional standards in teaching
functions.quote: Our role is to protect the public by promoting and regulating professional standards in teaching.

functions.what: fitness to teach, stated to be for the benefit of pupils and students
functions.quote: The Teaching Council is responsible for promoting high professional standards in teaching, for the benefit of pupils and students, and the profession.

functions.what: administers vetting of teachers
functions.quote: It is the role of the Teaching Council to administer vetting for teachers in Ireland.

bodies.notes: Read the Council's own home page (curl, full text); /about-us/ returned 404 so the homepage navigation text was used. The page names no establishing Act. Children are reached only via teachers in schools. Verdict part rests on the stated 'benefit of pupils and students' and the child-related vetting role; the NI equivalent (GTCNI) was coded none, so this is a consistency decision for the user (see openQuestions).

bodies.name: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (CICA)
bodies.universeName: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse (CICA)

functions.what: statutory basis and date established
functions.quote: was established on 23 May, 2000, pursuant to the "Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse Act 2000"

functions.quote: to conduct an inquiry into abuse of children in institutions during that period

bodies.statute: Commission to Inquire into Child Abuse Act 2000 (named on the Department's page)
bodies.notes: HISTORICAL scope: the inquiry concerns abuse in childhood in institutions 'from 1940 or earlier, to the present day' as the Department's page puts the period; no remit for current children. The body's own site childabusecommission.ie returned HTTP 500 (PHP error), so the Department's 'Bodies under the aegis' page (Internet Archive copy 2026-01-05, 'Last updated on 1 September 2022') is the fallback source. Whether the Commission still exists as a live body was not established. roles left empty: none of the nine role words fits an inquiry (see openQuestions). Verdict part follows the NI precedent for historical-abuse bodies (COSICA, HIA Redress Board).

bodies.name: Education and Training Boards (16, treated as one class)

functions.what: statutory function: establish and maintain recognised schools
functions.quote: establish and maintain recognised schools, centres for education and education or training facilities in its functional area

functions.what: statutory function: youth work services in the ETB's area
functions.quote: support the provision, coordination, administration and assessment of youth work services in its functional area

functions.what: ETBI (the ETBs' association) restates that youth work is an ETB responsibility under the 2013 Act
functions.quote: Education and Training Boards are charged with responsibility for Youth Work in the ETB 2013 Act

functions.what: ETBs are a delivery partner for the UBU youth funding scheme
functions.quote: The Education and Training Boards (ETB) works with the DCYA, as a strategic partner, to deliver UBU Your Place Your Space across the country.

functions.what: ETB Youth Officers support, develop and monitor local youth services
functions.quote: The ETB Youth Officers play a crucial role supporting, developing and monitoring their local youth services.

bodies.statute: Education and Training Boards Act 2013, section 10 (functions); youth work as defined in the Youth Work Act 2001 (section 10(6), as printed)
bodies.notes: Class entry for the 16 ETBs (universe lists 'Educational Training Boards' plus 16 named boards: Cavan and Monaghan; City of Dublin; Cork; Donegal; Dublin and Dun Laoghaire; Galway and Roscommon; Kerry; Kildare and Wicklow; Kilkenny and Carlow; Laois and Offaly; Limerick and Clare; Longford and Westmeath; Louth and Meath; Mayo, Sligo and Leitrim; Tipperary; Waterford and Wexford). Primary evidence is the Act (Irish Statute Book, section 10 as enacted; 'Minister for Children and Youth Affairs' and 'DCYA' are the 2013-era and UBU-page names, superseded by the 2025 reorganisation under which the Department of Education and Youth holds youth work). ETBI pages and the ubu.gov.ie ETB page confirm the youth role in current practice. The ubu.gov.ie page says ETBs work with the department to 'deliver' the scheme; it does NOT say that ETBs hold or distribute the funding, so 'funds' is NOT recorded as a role. ETBs also run schools (Community Colleges are ETB-established per the Department's policy page) and, per the Act, provide education in children detention schools. SOLAS (further education and training) was not read: it is adult-oriented and not needed for the youth question. One ETB's own site (Kerry ETB, kerryetb.ie/schools-youth-music/youth-services/) was opened and lists a 'Youth Clubs Grants Scheme' registration page, but the text read did not say who funds it, so it is not recorded. via is null because the youth-work function does not run through schools.

functions.what: child protection procedures apply to primary and post-primary schools
functions.quote: The Department of Education and Youth is responsible for developing and implementing child protection procedures for schools

bodies.notes: One class entry for the two universe rows 'Schools: State funded primary' and 'Schools: State funded post primary' (both sponsor Department of Education). Read the Department's Education policy page and child-protection page (Internet Archive copies of gov.ie, dates in the URLs); individual schools not researched. The Department page also says 'Most children attend state-funded schools'. Children are reached through schools by definition, hence via 'schools'; verdict core because the whole remit is the education of children and young people.

openQuestions: Teaching Council: coded part/via schools on the strength of 'for the benefit of pupils and students' and its vetting role. The NI equivalent (GTCNI) was coded none. Same treatment for both, or keep Ireland as part?
NCCA and SEC: coded part (NCCA via null because its remit includes early childhood education; SEC via schools). NI's CCEA was part/schools. Is NCCA's early-childhood reach enough to leave via null?

CICA and RIRB (historical abuse): per your NI ruling I was to include them only if there are corresponding voluntary-sector organisations. I cannot assess that from this batch (no voluntary-sector universe was in the brief), so both are recorded normally as part with HISTORICAL scope; decide whether to keep them in the Ireland children's-sector list. CICA's roles are empty because none of the nine role words fits an inquiry: add 'investigates', or leave blank?
CICA: the Department page describing it is 'Last updated on 1 September 2022' and CICA's own site is down (HTTP 500). Is it still a live body? Not established.

Department of Education and Youth: youth work/UBU sits there; early learning and childcare and school-age childcare sit with the Department of Children, Disability and Equality, which will need its own entry (it is not in my batch). The exact 2025 transfer order was not read; the split rests on the two departments' own current pages.

ETBs as a class: the youth-work function is statutory (Act s.10) and they deliver UBU with the Department, but I could not confirm from a source that ETBs hold or distribute the youth funding streams, so no 'funds' role was recorded. Worth a targeted check of an ETB youth-services page or the UBU funding guidelines in the money stage.

Leargas is not in the CSO universe (charity / company limited by guarantee) and its sponsor is the Department of Further and Higher Education, not Education. Keep it in this children's-sector list as part, or move/drop it?

gov.ie (AWS WAF), ncca.ie and examinations.ie (Cloudflare) refuse automated access, so Department pages were read through Internet Archive copies. If you want live-URL citations for those, a manual fetch in a normal browser would be needed.
